exposure: Neonatal metabolome (specifically cyclo-leucine-proline and 5-aminovaleric acid betaine)
Genetic variants near SLC22A4 and SLC22A5 (in adults)
cohort: The study included over 1400 Danish newborns, later diagnosed with autism and matching controls, from a population-based cohort (iPSYCH2015), as well as over 7000 adult participants from two Swedish population-based cohorts.
finding: Cyclo-leucine-proline and 5-aminovaleric acid betaine (5-AVAB) in the neonatal metabolome were associated with a future diagnosis of autism in Danish neonates, independently of known prenatal and genetic risk factors.
followup_time: Extensive, linking neonatal blood spots collected shortly after birth to autism diagnosis later in childhood and adulthood (for Swedish cohorts).
